#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: -N 1
#flux: --ntasks-per-node=1
#flux: -t 12:00:00

# The original script did not specify cpus-per-task, so it defaults to 1.
# This is preserved by not specifying a '-c' or '--cpus-per-task' option.

# CRITICAL: The following resource requests from Slurm could not be translated and have been OMITTED.
# These are highly site-specific. This job will likely FAIL without them.
# The job will NOT be allocated a GPU and will NOT be allocated 20GB of memory.
# #SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
# #SBATCH --mem=20GB


module load pytorch/1.4.0-py36-cuda90
module load torchvision/0.5.0-py36

#pip install geoopt
#pip install git+https://github.com/geoopt/geoopt.git

# The python command is run directly, as this is a single-task job.
python3 pvae/main.py --model mnist --manifold PoincareBall --c 0.1  --latent-dim 40 --hidden-dim 600 --prior WrappedNormal --posterior WrappedNormal --dec Geo     --enc Wrapped --lr 5e-4 --epochs 80 --save-freq 80 --batch-size 128 --iwae-samples 5000

reasons: Validation failed at directive: --ntasks-per-node=1. The standard short-form option ('-n 1' for a single node job) is more portable and widely supported.
issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, two essential resource requests from the original Slurm script were omitted: the request for a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) and the request for 20GB of memory (`--mem=20GB`). While the translated script is syntactically valid (aside from the reason noted above), it is functionally incorrect. It will not be allocated a GPU and will receive a default, likely insufficient, memory allocation. Both omissions will almost certainly cause the job to fail at runtime.
